anchors.prompt: Create a new photo: A small sunny back patio of a modest family house in the late morning: a whitewashed wall with potted herbs in terracotta pots, a clothesline with a few towels, a small white plastic table with a tube of sunscreen, a wide-brimmed straw hat and a glass of water; the glass door to the kitchen on the right; bright even daylight. The doctor stands in the patio next to the little table, looking at the viewer mid-sentence. Medium shot, waist up, from about two meters. The man is the doctor of the input image (a close-up of his real face): EXACTLY that face — same face shape, eyes, nose, eyebrows, dark curly hair with a little grey, short salt-and-pepper beard, same age (about 40) — do not make him younger or more handsome. He wears blue medical scrubs with short sleeves, a black stethoscope around his neck and a black smartwatch on his left wrist. A casual home video frame, ordinary, candid.
Same place, same framing and same light: he stands with a serious, honest face, hands open.
Same place, same framing and same light: he stands in the sun shading his eyes with one hand.
Same place, same framing and same light: he holds the tube of sunscreen toward the camera.
Same place, same framing and same light: he holds up three fingers, serious.
Same place, same framing and same light: he holds the tube against his chest, calm smile.

EXTREME CLOSE-UP of his HANDS ONLY in bright daylight: a line of white sunscreen squeezed along his index and middle fingers, the tube in the other hand. No face —  Same place, same light and same objects as the first image, but the camera is now VERY CLOSE: this detail fills the whole frame.
Same close-up: his fingers spread the white sunscreen over the back of his other hand.
Same place, same framing and same light: he rubs the backs of his hands together, looking at the viewer.
Same place, same framing and same light: he holds both hands up with the backs toward the camera.
Same place, same framing and same light: he wears the wide-brimmed straw hat, smiling.
Same place, same framing and same light: he points at his left cheek, eyebrows raised.
Same place, same framing and same light: he holds the amber bottle, the hat on the table, calm.
Same place, same framing and same light: he shakes his head with a warning face.
Same place, same framing and same light: he stands with one hand on his chest, sincere.
Same place, same framing and same light: he stands at the glass kitchen door, one hand on the handle, looking back at the viewer.

clips.text: Las manchas. Te voy a decir la verdad, aunque no sea lo que quieres escuchar: ningún aceite casero aclara una mancha. Ninguno. Tampoco el de laurel.
clips.action: He talks honestly to the camera, shaking his head slightly, hands open.

clips.text: ¿Sabes qué es lo que más las oscurece? El sol. El de todos los días: ir al mercado, colgar la ropa, manejar con el brazo en la ventana.
clips.action: He points up at the sky, mimes hanging laundry on the line, and rests an arm as if on a car window.

clips.text: Así que el verdadero antimanchas cuesta poco y está en la farmacia: protector solar, todas las mañanas, aunque esté nublado.
clips.action: He picks up the tube of sunscreen from the little table and shows it to the camera.

clips.text: Y las manchas que ya tienes, las de muchos años, no se van con nada de la cocina. Ni con limón, ni con bicarbonato, ni con agua oxigenada. Eso irrita, y mancha más.
clips.action: He shakes his head and counts on his fingers, the sunscreen tube in the other hand.

clips.text: Lo que sí hace el protector, con constancia, es que no aparezcan nuevas, y que las de ahora no se oscurezcan más. Y eso ya es muchísimo.
clips.action: He nods slowly, holding the sunscreen tube against his chest.

clips.text: Una cantidad como de dos dedos, para la cara y el cuello. Y aquí viene lo que casi nadie hace: el dorso de las manos.
clips.action: EXTREME CLOSE-UP of the HANDS ONLY: white sunscreen is squeezed along two fingers, then spread over the back of the other hand.

clips.text: Las manos delatan la edad antes que la cara. ¿Y sabes por qué? Porque nadie se pone protector en las manos. Treinta segundos, y listo.
clips.action: He shows the backs of his hands to the camera, turning them slowly.

clips.text: Si vas a estar afuera, te vuelves a poner después de lavarte las manos. Y un sombrero de ala ancha, que es el protector que nunca falla.
clips.action: He picks up the wide-brimmed straw hat, puts it on and adjusts it with a smile.

clips.text: Y el manejo, eh. La mano izquierda y el lado izquierdo de la cara reciben sol por la ventana del auto. Por eso a muchos se les mancha más un lado.
clips.action: Wearing the hat, he mimes holding a steering wheel with his left elbow out, then points at the left side of his face.

clips.text: Ahora, ¿qué papel juega el aceite de laurel con las manchas? Uno pequeño, y honesto: hidrata. Y la piel hidratada se ve más pareja, más luminosa.
clips.action: He takes off the hat, picks up the small amber bottle from the table and speaks calmly.

clips.text: Pero ojo con esto: el aceite, de noche. Nunca antes de salir al sol. Y nada de ponerle limón al aceite, que con el sol mancha más.
clips.action: He wags his finger, mimes squeezing a lemon, and shakes his head.

clips.text: Y si una mancha de la cara te molesta mucho, eso se habla con un dermatólogo: hay tratamientos de verdad. Pero en casa, primero, el protector.
clips.action: He speaks seriously, one hand on his chest.

clips.text: Para el dorso de las manos te dejo algo más, bien sencillo: un exfoliante de azúcar con el mismo aceite. Vamos al fregadero.
clips.action: He walks toward the glass kitchen door, inviting the viewer to follow.
